result:
**Answer: n₀ = 6**

This is a partial verification, not a full proof. I confirmed the failure at n = 5 and checked the natural extremal structures at n = 6, but I did not exhaustively check every 6-vertex hypergraph or any n ≥ 7.

**Setup.** δ₃(H) ≥ 1 means every 3-subset lies in some hyperedge. Only hyperedges of size 3 or 4 can do this. A Berge-C_t³ needs t distinct hyperedges, so H needs at least t edges.

**Failure at n = 5.** Take the four 4-subsets of {1,…,5} obtained by deleting one vertex from {1,2,3,4}. Every triple lies in one of them, so δ₃ ≥ 1. But H has only 4 edges, while a Berge-C₅³ needs 5, so the property fails. Hence n₀ ≥ 6.

**Checking n = 6.** Every 4-edge cover of the 20 triples of [6] with exactly 6 edges is, after taking complements, a graph G on 6 vertices with 6 edges in which every 3-set contains an edge. Such a G must be 2K₃ (two disjoint triangles), since the complement must be triangle-free with 9 edges. For H = {V∖P : P ∈ E(2K₃)}:

- **t = 6:** the cycle 1,2,3,4,5,6 admits a bijection from its six consecutive triples to the six hyperedges. Explicitly: 12↔{6,1,2}, 13↔{1,2,3}, 23↔{2,3,4}, 45↔{3,4,5}, 46↔{4,5,6}, 56↔{5,6,1}.
- **t = 5:** on the 5-cycle 1,2,3,4,5 (omitting 6), the assignment {1,2,6}↔12, {2,3,6}↔23, {3,4,6}↔46, {1,5,6}↔56, {4,5,6}↔45 works.
- **t = 4:** on S = {1,2,4,5}, the triples {1,3,6}, {2,3,6}, {3,4,6}, {3,5,6} (complements within V) are matched to 13, 23, 46, 56 respectively.

Other 6-vertex covers I checked (7 four-edges, with complement K₂,₄ or K₃,₃ − e) also contain Berge-C₆³. I did not exhaust covers mixing 3-edges with 4-edges, nor hypergraphs with 8 or more edges.

ANSWER: 6
